feedback.answered: Initial backbone: A1 support is collected as voter responses and per-peer matched log indexes. send queues vote and append responses, including self responses, behind persistence; RawNode delivers external responses through Ready or local storage messages, and synchronous Advance steps self responses. ProgressTracker selects voting members and JointConfig requires both constituent majorities. maybeCommit combines that index with the current term. Followers match the preceding entry before appending and cap commit by the received matching suffix; committed conflicts panic. A2 authority is term/state dependent: campaigns require promotability and no unapplied committed configuration changes, pre-campaign does not increment term, elections reset vote accounting, and becoming leader resets progress and appends an empty entry. Step filters older-term responses and normally relinquishes authority on higher terms, with explicit pre-vote and leader-lease exceptions. Thus old replication support is not simply carried into new leadership, whereas committed history and snapshot state survive authority changes. Async entry-stability responses carry the producing term; stale responses do not stabilize entries, but snapshot completion is still processed. A4 configuration changes replace the quorum context used by A1, and restored snapshots reconstruct membership. A5/A6 consumption crosses Ready/Advance or ordered local append/apply queues; the application owns actual durable writes and state-machine application. These are source observations and interface duties, not executed evidence.

formation.explanation: Leader proposals acquire current term/index and enter the unstable log. Self and follower append acknowledgments wait for caller persistence before contributing Match support. Voting membership selects the majority order statistic (both majorities in joint mode); maybeCommit additionally requires the selected entry to have the current leader term. Append broadcasts propagate new commit, while heartbeats cap it by each follower Match. Followers check the previous entry and prevent committed-prefix overwrite. Ready exposes committed entries in order; snapshot and application quota can delay delivery. Caller application and Advance or async responses update application bookkeeping.

context.explanation: A promotable node without unapplied committed configuration changes can campaign. Pre-vote does not change term; real candidacy increments term and persists votes, and only current voting quorum support wins. Winning leadership resets follower progress, appends an empty entry and begins replication. Step normally relinquishes authority on higher term and rejects old replies; pre-vote and lease exceptions are explicit. Same-term leader messages displace candidates. CheckQuorum can step down. Transfer suppresses proposals until a caught-up voter receives TimeoutNow, with timeout abort and normal election safeguards. Removal can optionally step down the leader.

connection.explanation: Membership qualifies both election and replication support. Term resets discard old match/vote/readOnly acknowledgment tracking; Step rejects stale responses, while previously committed history remains binding. Entry stability acknowledgments retain the producing term to avoid discarding a replaced unstable suffix; old snapshot completions remain meaningful because snapshots carry committed state. Restart loads durable history/configuration and enters follower state. Pending pre-commit reads live separately from the reset readOnly queue and are released on response-based current-term commit. Applied membership may reinterpret existing matches and produce a commit without that same read-release callback. Application completion can propose automatic joint exit, but transfer admission can reject that proposal; these local continuation questions do not prevent understanding the backbone.

feedback.answered: Initial backbone: A1 support is collected as voter responses and per-peer matched log indexes. send queues vote and append responses, including self responses, behind persistence; RawNode delivers external responses through Ready or local storage messages, and synchronous Advance steps self responses. ProgressTracker selects voting members and JointConfig requires both constituent majorities. maybeCommit combines that index with the current term. Followers match the preceding entry before appending and cap commit by the received matching suffix; committed conflicts panic. A2 authority is term/state dependent: campaigns require promotability and no unapplied committed configuration changes, pre-campaign does not increment term, elections reset vote accounting, and becoming leader resets progress and appends an empty entry. Step filters older-term responses and normally relinquishes authority on higher terms, with explicit pre-vote and leader-lease exceptions. Thus old replication support is not simply carried into new leadership, whereas committed history and snapshot state survive authority changes. Async entry-stability responses carry the producing term; stale responses do not stabilize entries, but snapshot completion is still processed. A4 configuration changes replace the quorum context used by A1, and restored snapshots reconstruct membership. A5/A6 consumption crosses Ready/Advance or ordered local append/apply queues; the application owns actual durable writes and state-machine application. These are source observations and interface duties, not executed evidence.

formation.explanation: Leader proposals acquire current term/index and enter the unstable log. Self and follower append acknowledgments wait for caller persistence before contributing Match support. Voting membership selects the majority order statistic (both majorities in joint mode); maybeCommit additionally requires the selected entry to have the current leader term. Append broadcasts propagate new commit, while heartbeats cap it by each follower Match. Followers check the previous entry and prevent committed-prefix overwrite. Ready exposes committed entries in order; snapshot and application quota can delay delivery. Caller application and Advance or async responses update application bookkeeping.

context.explanation: A promotable node without unapplied committed configuration changes can campaign. Pre-vote does not change term; real candidacy increments term and persists votes, and only current voting quorum support wins. Winning leadership resets follower progress, appends an empty entry and begins replication. Step normally relinquishes authority on higher term and rejects old replies; pre-vote and lease exceptions are explicit. Same-term leader messages displace candidates. CheckQuorum can step down. Transfer suppresses proposals until a caught-up voter receives TimeoutNow, with timeout abort and normal election safeguards. Removal can optionally step down the leader.

connection.explanation: Membership qualifies both election and replication support. Term resets discard old match/vote/readOnly acknowledgment tracking; Step rejects stale responses, while previously committed history remains binding. Entry stability acknowledgments retain the producing term to avoid discarding a replaced unstable suffix; old snapshot completions remain meaningful because snapshots carry committed state. Restart loads durable history/configuration and enters follower state. Pending pre-commit reads live separately from the reset readOnly queue and are released on response-based current-term commit. Applied membership may reinterpret existing matches and produce a commit without that same read-release callback. Application completion can propose automatic joint exit, but transfer admission can reject that proposal; these local continuation questions do not prevent understanding the backbone.
